header:
Date: 2026-04-18
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Redwood CSM), Priya Shah (SolarFlare Head of ML), Ethan Cole (CTO), Marisol Vega (Platform Eng), Daniel Cho (FinOps)
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost reduction levers, reliability incidents over last quarter, and alignment on roadmap + pilot for Dedicated capacity. Customer interested in Private/VPC questions and SOC2 evidence; agreed to run latency benchmarks and share pricing options.
topics: Usage trends and monthly token volumes
Roadmap alignment and Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining for the QBR. I see most of the folks on the call, we'll go through usage, costs, reliability then roadmap.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Thanks, yes, excited to get into it. We had a big uptick in chat volume in March so curious about cost levers.
[00:28] Marco Diaz: Quick agenda — I'll share the recent benchmark, then Lena will cover pricing, Aisha for adoption health.
[00:35] Ethan Cole: Quick add — we want a status on the SOC2 artifacts, and also whether a private deployment affects latency.
[00:44] Aisha Rahman: Noted. Priya, can you confirm the main success criteria — is it latency under 200ms p95 and 35% cost reduction?
[00:52] Priya Shah: That's right, p95 under 200 for web flows and cost down 30-40% via batching/quant.
[01:05] Marco Diaz: Alright, sharing screen — benchmark spreadsheet link posted in chat: https://redwood.link/benchmarks-ss23 (note: link is shorthand). Our end-to-end numbers from last week: hosted gen for 2k concurrent users median token lat 120ms when cached, p95 around 260ms for long sequences.
[01:30] Marisol Vega: That p95 is higher than we expected, we saw service spikes last month during promo. Any idea cause?
[01:40] Marco Diaz: Looking at traces, a couple of spikes were due to cold KV cache misses and oversized payloads hitting the runtime. There's also a region failover where requests routed to a higher-latency instance.
[01:55] Daniel Cho: On cost — our FinOps run shows tokens spiked by 60% and monthly spend jumped. We need clear levers.
[02:05] Lena Park: Yes, the common levers are: smarter batching, prefix/KV caching, quantized model variants, and Dedicated pools with predictable throughput. For your profile we recommended a mix: keep critical traffic on hosted, move background generation to Dedicated.
[02:30] Priya Shah: Can Dedicated help with p95?
[02:34] Marco Diaz: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pool and lower tail latency because you're not sharing queue capacity. We saw p95 drop by ~30-40% in similar customers after tuning batch sizes. There is also Redwood Optimize suggestions — quick config changes we can propose.
[02:55] Ethan Cole: Is there a tradeoff in cost for Dedicated?
[02:58] Lena Park: Dedicated is commit-based; higher fixed cost but lower per-token for heavy sustained throughput. We modeled two scenarios in the sheet — I'll send the pricing.
[03:12] Marco Diaz: Also note private deployment options — VPC and on-prem. Private removes network egress variability but you lose some of the autoscaling elasticity unless you add burst capacity.
[03:26] Marisol Vega: For VPC, how does KMS integration work? We have a managed HSM with strict audit rules.
[03:32] Aisha Rahman: We support KMS/HSM integrations, and you can bring your own keys. We'll share the SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration guide after the call.
[03:44] Priya Shah: Good. On the incidents — we had two reliability incidents in March, what was the root cause?
[03:50] Marco Diaz: One was a model load race during a rollout — the canary didn't get the new quant profile and caused OOMs on a few nodes, we fixed rollback policy. The other was region throttling; requests bounced to a secondary region with different model variant causing mismatch and latency.
[04:10] Ethan Cole: Is there an automatic fallback policy you recommend to avoid variant mismatch?
[04:15] Marco Diaz: Yes, Smart routing can automatically fall back to a compatible variant in the same region tier. We can configure stricter model-compatibility rules to avoid that mismatch.
[04:28] Daniel Cho: We're also interested in unit economics — can batching & quantization realistically drop our monthly spend by 30%?
[04:35] Marco Diaz: In our tests, quantizing to int8 and enabling prefix caching yielded 25-45% savings depending on sequence distribution. For SolarFlare's mix — more short chat turns — batching gives less than for long generations but KV cache helps a lot.
[04:55] Priya Shah: Any quality regressions with quant? We care about hallucinations in rerank tasks.
[05:02] Marco Diaz: Good callout. We recommend a quality gating: run A/B evals on a holdout prompt set; Redwood Optimize can automatically flag regressions and rollback. We can run a quick eval for your rerank set in the pilot.
[05:18] Priya Shah: Sounds good.
[05:20] Aisha Rahman: Quick health metrics — adoption up 18% q/q, active routes increased from 6 to 9, but error rate was 0.8% in March due to the incidents noted.
[05:32] Marisol Vega: 0.8% is acceptable but we need root cause and mitigations.
[05:36] Marco Diaz: Mitigations: stricter rollout windows, automated canary verification, KV cache warmers during deployments, and region-aware routing.
[05:46] Ethan Cole: On security, Priya wants SOC2 evidence and maybe penetration test summary — can you provide?
[05:52] Lena Park: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II report excerpt and TAS penetration summary under NDA. Also SSO/SAML docs.
[05:58] Daniel Cho: For procurement — if we go Dedicated, what's the contract length and exit terms?
[06:03] Lena Park: Standard is 12-month commitments for Dedicated with monthly invoices; exit terms depend on commitment level — I'll include the contract template in the pricing email.
[06:12] Priya Shah: Roadmap alignment — we're planning a feature for real-time product suggestions by Q3. Can Redwood support lower-latency inference for that use case?
[06:21] Marco Diaz: Yes, that's a good fit for Dedicated or Private with local inference. For strict latency we'd recommend a private VPC deployment colocated in your region, with pre-warmed KV caches.
[06:35] Marisol Vega: We also need network egress budgeting — will VPC peering increase our costs?
[06:40] Lena Park: There may be egress charges from cloud providers for cross-region traffic. We can model that in the cost worksheet.
[06:48] Marco Diaz: I'm going to walk through a short tech diagram setup — posting a whiteboard link in chat. (brief screen share)
[07:00] Marco Diaz: Diagram: public hosted endpoints -> smart routing -> dedicated pools or private VPC; prefix cache sits at routing tier. Note: I may have said KV cash earlier in chat, my bad.
[07:18] Priya Shah: Ha, KV cash, yes.
[07:20] Ethan Cole: On benchmarking — what exact workload should we use? We'll pick a representative sample but what size?
[07:27] Marco Diaz: 10k sample requests covering short chat, product-suggestion long form, and rerank flows. Include worst-case length examples. Priya to provide the sample set.
[07:40] Priya Shah: I'll prepare and upload to the shared drive.
[07:44] Marco Diaz: Great. Also for the pilot, we'll propose a two-week Dedicated trial with a small reserved pool and telemetry hooks to compare p95 and cost.
[07:55] Daniel Cho: A trial with clear KPIs is fine. We'll want billing transparency so we can reconcile during trial.
[08:02] Lena Park: We'll enable token-level billing breakdown and route-level dashboards for the trial.
[08:10] Aisha Rahman: Quick note on action items — I'll set up the follow-up meeting and invite the infra folks.
[08:16] Marisol Vega: Two questions from me: 1) How quickly can you share the SOC2 redaction? 2) Do you support cross-account VPC peering?
[08:25] Lena Park: SOC2 under NDA, we can share within 48 hours. Cross-account VPC peering is supported, yes — we'll provide the network runbook.
[08:34] Ethan Cole: Any competitors we should be worried about offering lower prices?
[08:36] Daniel Cho: We've seen marketing from OpenAI and Anthropic on pricing but their enterprise features vary.
[08:42] Marco Diaz: We differentiate on predictable serving economics and operational tooling — Redwood Console, rollouts, tracer hooks.
[08:50] Priya Shah: Ok can we get a side-by-side of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for our use-case?
[08:55] Lena Park: Yes, I'll include that in the pricing email with modeled costs and expected p95 improvements.
[09:03] Marco Diaz: Anything else on reliability?
[09:06] Marisol Vega: Just that we need a postmortem for the March incident.
[09:09] Marco Diaz: We'll attach a short postmortem with remediation steps.
[09:14] Priya Shah: Great. Last bit — timeline: we want pilot in May, ramp in June if results good.
[09:22] Lena Park: Sounds good. I'll coordinate with legal and procurement to fast-track Dedicated contract if pilot meets KPIs.
[09:30] Aisha Rahman: I'll send calendar invites for the follow-up: bench run review (Apr 21), pricing & contract review (Apr 22), infra deep dive (week of Apr 27).
[09:40] Daniel Cho: Thanks, team.
[09:45] Lena Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.
[09:50] (meeting ends)
